sentences.text:
Chandan Singh Verma vs State Of U.P. & Anr. on 23 November,
2020

Author: Alok Mathur
Bench: Alok Mathur
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 29
Case :- U/S 482/378/407 No. - 2631 of 2020
Applicant :- Chandan Singh Verma
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. & Anr.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Asarey Verma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Alok Mathur,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. By means of the present applicant the applicant has sought quashing the criminal proceedings of Case No.14 of 2020 (State Vs. Chandan Singh Verma) under Section 18 (a)/28 and 18 (c)/27(b) II of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, Police Station Neemgaon, District Lakhimpur Kheri as well as the summoning order dated 29.1.2020.

entities.text: Case No.14 of 2020 (State Vs. Chandan Singh Verma)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Police Station Neemgaon, District Lakhimpur Kheri
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the applicant is running a medical store styled as M/s Verma Medical Store, Bhupatipur Road, Gadariya, Chauraha, Police Station - Neemgaon, Distric Kheri.

According to the applicant a raid was conducted on 13.7.2018 at the said medical store by a team consisting of police officials as well as officials of Drugs and Cosmetics Department, State of U.P. and it was found that the applicant was conducting the Chandan Singh Verma vs State Of U.P. & Anr. on 23 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11523761/
1 business in selling drugs and cosmetics without proper license nor was he able to produce any such license to the raiding party.

entities.text: Drugs and Cosmetics Department, State of U.P.
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Chandan Singh Verma vs State Of U.P. & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was stated that despite a notice having been issued to him earlier, he could not submit any document for running his business during the said raid.
It has been submitted that the drugs being sold by him were also seized in accordance with the rules framed therein.

Thereafter an F.I.R. was registered on 13.7.2018 in case crime No.190 of 2018, under Sections- 419,
420 of IPC and 18 (A), 18 (c), 27 (b) (ii), 28 of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 at police station Neemgaon, District Lakhimpur Kheri.

4. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that his grievance for which he has approached this Court is with regard to the proceedings initiated by the State in pursuance of the complaint moved by Drug Inspector, Food Safety and Drug Administration, Office of District Magistrate, Lakhimpur Kheri wherein it has been mentioned that the premises of the applicant was raided on 13.7.2018 in which it was found that the applicant was conducting the business without any license and further that on the said date certain drugs mentioned in para 7 of Annexure No.2 were seized.

entities.text: Food Safety and Drug Administration, Office of District Magistrate, Lakhimpur Kheri
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The drugs were further sent to the State Public Analysis Laboratory, U.P. Aliganj,
Lucknow which has reported that the said drugs were adulterated and, therefore, as a consequence of the said complaint criminal proceedings and summoning order dated 29.1.2020, which have been impugned in the present case, have been issued.

entities.text: State Public Analysis Laboratory, U.P. Aliganj
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The only ground urged by the applicant is that prosecution on the same set of facts has been taken on the basis of an F.I.R., then proceedings in the compliant case should not have been undertaken and this is violative of Article 20 of the Constitution of India and, therefore, has prayed that the present proceedings b set aside.
5.

Learned A.G.A., on the hand, has vehemently opposed the petition and submitted that facts in both cases are very different and the offence under which the applicant has been charged are different and, therefore, there is no basis for allowing the petition of the petitioner.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.

7. From the aforesaid facts it is clear that the first information report was lodged on 13.7.2018 for the raid conducted on the premises of the medical store of the applicant wherein the only charge pertains was with regard to his conducting business without license of drugs and cosmetics without proper license and, therefore, F.I.R. under Section 18 (A), 18 (c), 27 (b) (ii) and 28 of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, has been lodged.

Aforesaid Sections provide as under:-"
"18 (c) Manufacture for sale or for distribution, or sell, or stock or exhibit or offer for sale or distribute any drug or cosmetic, except under and in accordance with the conditions of a license issued for such purpose under this Chapter:
18-A. Disclosure of the name of the manufacture, etc.:- Every person, not being the manufacturer of a drug or cosmetic or his agent for the distribution thereof, shall, if so required, disclose to the Inspector the name, address and other particulars of the person from whom he acquired the drug or cosmetic.
27. Penalty for manufacture, sale, etc., of drugs in contravention of this Chapter:
Chandan Singh Verma vs State Of U.P. & Anr. on 23 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11523761/
2 (b) any drug (i) .......or (ii) without a valid license as required under clause (c) of section 18, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees or three times the value of the drugs confiscated, whichever is more."
28. Penalty for non-disclosure of the name of the manufacturer, etc.:-

entities.text: Chandan Singh Verma vs State Of U.P. & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 18-A [or section 24] shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which shall not be less than twenty thousand rupees or with both."
8.

From the aforesaid Sections it is clear that the matter pertains squarely to non- mentioning of the name of manufacturer and for selling of the drugs without proper license, and, as such, the present criminal proceedings have arisen on the basis of the report of the Drug Inspector dated 3.1.2019 which after examining and analyzing held that the said drugs were adulterated or did not prescribe to the standard norms.
9.

From a perusal of the both the proceedings initiated against the applicant it is clear that they are distinct and and different and there is no legal impediment on both proceedings going on simultaneously as they relate to two separate offences and charges.
From the above, it is absolutely clear that there is no violation of Article 20 of the Constitution.
10. In view of above, there is no merit in the contentions raised by counsel for the applicant.
The application being without merits is accordingly dismissed.

Order Date :- 23.11.2020 (Alok Mathur, J.)
RKM.
